name: CID HoldCo, Inc. (Dot Ai)

profile.description: CID HoldCo, Inc., operating as Dot Ai, is a Las Vegas-based micro-cap that went public via SPAC in June 2025 selling IoT asset-tracking hardware and AI-enhanced analytics software, and is attempting a shift to subscription revenue. In October 2026 it closed a ~$65M all-stock acquisition of Envoy Technologies, an all-electric car-sharing amenity provider, from BladeRanger, partly to restore Nasdaq's stockholders' equity requirement; Envoy's $12.5M convertible note held by Blink Charging remains outstanding. The company faces a Nasdaq delisting determination (hearing pending), executed a 1-for-25 reverse split in May 2026, reported Q2 2026 revenue of only $12,398 (-90% YoY), and disclosed a secured-loan default that could lead to foreclosure on a material portion of its assets. Market cap is roughly $2.5-2.7M at $1.05/share.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): The company has attempted a hardware-to-subscription pivot and has now bolted on Envoy's EV car-sharing business, but revenue collapsed from $5.8M in FY2025 to about $25K in H1 2026 and the Envoy deal was explicitly framed around Nasdaq equity compliance rather than a proven product success [1][2]. AI Deployment (1/2): Dot Ai markets AI-enhanced asset-intelligence analytics, but with Q1/Q2 2026 revenue of $12,214 and $12,398 there are no measurable customer results or quantified savings [1]. Market Share (0/2): A sub-$3M market-cap participant with no share data in a crowded IoT/asset-tracking market. Product Pipeline (0/2): Management reaffirmed 2026 revenue guidance of $6.0-7.5M and $12-15M bookings back-end weighted into H2 [1], but no named next-generation products with launch dates were disclosed. R&D Intensity (0/1): No reliable R&D-to-revenue comparison is available; spending is constrained by a secured-loan default [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): Dot Ai describes itself as an 'asset intelligence' company providing real-time visibility into assets and operations — a generic technology positioning, now muddied by the addition of an unrelated EV car-sharing business [2][4]. Community Impact (0/2): No charitable or community programs were found. Employee Retention (0/2): With 68 employees, a secured-loan default and possible foreclosure on a material portion of operations [3], there is no evidence of retention strength. Insider Buying (0/2): No open-market insider purchases were identified; equity changes have come through SPAC, reverse split and all-stock acquisition issuance [2][3].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on growth-stock metrics, every available metric scores zero. Stockholders' equity is negative (book value of -$4.30/share per FMP), so debt-to-equity is not meaningful and is scored at the floor (0.0); the yfinance D/E figure of 16.6% is disregarded because it does not reflect the deficit [5]. ROE of -79.1% (0.0, 2x weight), revenue growth of -90% YoY in Q2 2026 (0.0) and a TTM net margin of about -277% (0.0) all sit at or below their floors [1][5]. Forward P/E and PEG are unavailable with no earnings, and the 5-year revenue CAGR is not meaningful for a 2025 SPAC with a sub-$1M revenue history; these are excluded. Weighted sum 0 / 5 = 0. Liquidity floor technically cleared on the reported 8.2M average volume (~$8.6M/day) [5], but recent daily volume of 120K-1.0M shares is near the $1M threshold.

ai_resilience.label: HIGH RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (4/9): Dot Ai's core offering — IoT tracking plus analytics software — sits in a category where large platforms (cloud providers, ERP and logistics software vendors) are embedding AI-driven asset visibility directly into their products, leaving a sub-scale point solution with little defensible data or switching cost [1][2]. The Envoy car-sharing business adds a physical-operations layer that AI cannot replace, which keeps the score from falling further, but that segment competes on fleet economics, not technology [2]. AI Opportunity (0/1): Despite the 'Ai' branding, the company reports no quantified AI revenue; total quarterly revenue in 2026 has been about $12K [1].

infinite_game.summary: Dot Ai is in survival mode: a pending Nasdaq delisting hearing, a 1-for-25 reverse split, a secured-loan default with possible foreclosure, and an all-stock acquisition driven by listing compliance. In Sinek's lens, every major decision of the past year has been about staying listed this quarter rather than advancing a cause, which is the definition of a finite player.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The company articulates an 'asset intelligence' purpose — continuous visibility into assets and operations [4] — but it is a product description rather than a vision of a better future, and the pivot into EV car-sharing shows it does not anchor strategy [2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): A 68-person organization facing a secured-loan default, delinquent-filing citation from Nasdaq and possible foreclosure on a material portion of its operations [3] cannot offer employees a Circle of Safety; no evidence of cultural strength was found.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary acknowledging or learning from competitors in IoT asset tracking or car-sharing was found; communications focus on listing compliance and deal closings [2][3].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (0/2): The hardware-to-subscription shift and Envoy acquisition are changes of direction, but Sinek distinguishes flexibility driven by a Just Cause from moves driven by desperation; the Envoy deal was explicitly tied to meeting Nasdaq's $2.5M stockholders' equity rule [2].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Leadership decisions in 2026 — the 1-for-25 reverse split, appeals of delisting determinations and an all-stock acquisition at a $6 reference price versus a ~$1 market price — protect the listing rather than sacrifice near-term outcomes for long-term capability [2][3].

investment_thesis: The only bull case is an option on a turnaround. Management reaffirmed 2026 guidance of $6.0-7.5M revenue and $12-15M bookings, implying a steep H2 ramp from H1 revenue of roughly $25K, and the October 2026 closing of the ~$65M Envoy acquisition adds an operating EV car-sharing business at residential, hotel and campus properties where Dot Ai's tracking technology could be applied [1][2]. If Nasdaq's Hearings Panel accepts the equity-compliance case and guidance is met, a ~$2.5M market cap leaves extreme upside on any stabilization.
thesis_continued: The bear case is existential. Nasdaq staff has determined to delist the stock on market-value grounds and added a delinquent-filing basis, the company is in default on a secured loan (about $1.06M owed as of August 12, 2026) with foreclosure expected to transfer a material portion of its assets, and Envoy brings a $12.5M convertible note held by Blink Charging [2][3]. Revenue fell 90% YoY in Q2 2026, equity is negative, and the 1-for-25 reverse split plus all-stock deal issuance at a $6 reference price against a ~$1 share price point to continued heavy dilution [3][5].
key_catalysts: Nasdaq Hearings Panel decision on whether the Envoy acquisition satisfies the $2.5M stockholders' equity requirement and resolves the market-value and delinquent-filing deficiencies [2][3]
Delivery of the back-end-weighted 2026 guidance ($6.0-7.5M revenue, $12-15M bookings) in the Q3 and Q4 reports [1]
Resolution of the LHT I, LLC secured-loan default without foreclosure on core operations [3]
key_risks: Delisting from Nasdaq following the August 6, 2026 staff determination and the added delinquent-filing basis, which would severely impair liquidity [3]
Foreclosure under the secured-loan default, which the company expects would transfer a material portion of its operations and assets [3]
Further dilution from Series C convertible preferred issued in the Envoy deal and the outstanding $12.5M Blink Charging convertible note [2]
